7f3bgk: An association received an unexpected offer: it could use a space free of charge for a year, but it had to take care of small repairs and open it to the neighborhood two afternoons a week. At the first meeting, some immediately imagined workshops, exhibitions, and a library of objects. Others remembered that the group already had trouble dividing up its current tasks.
10ohx1j: The coordinator proposed discussing a different question: «Si aceptáramos, ¿qué dejaríamos de hacer?». She didn't want to dampen the enthusiasm, but to relate it to the available time. If everyone could contribute four more hours, the project would be simple; in reality, many people worked or cared for relatives. One participant suggested sharing the space with another association. That would reduce the work, although it would require negotiating schedules and storage.
103dudv: The group drew up two scenarios. In the first they accepted the whole space and suspended one monthly activity. In the second they proposed using it just one afternoon, with a smaller commitment. Neither option was perfect. They decided to ask the owner whether he would accept a three-month trial before committing for a year. Imagining possibilities let them discover desires, but also limits. The final question stopped being «¿nos gustaría tener un local?» and became «¿qué proyecto podemos sostener sin agotar a quienes lo hacen posible?».
